Agent

The agent module contains the core ReAct (Reason + Act) agent implementation.

Core Agent

Core agent implementation using the ReAct pattern.

This module provides the main Agent class that orchestrates the Thought → Action → Observation loop using LLM and tools.

exception aria.agent.core.AgentError[source]

Bases: Exception

Exception raised when agent execution fails.

class aria.agent.core.Agent(client, registry, console, approval_handler=None, max_iterations=10, conversation_store=None)[source]

Bases: object

ARIA agent implementing the ReAct pattern.

The agent follows the Thought → Action → Observation → Thought cycle: 1. Receives user input and analyzes it 2. Calls LLM to decide on actions (tool use or direct response) 3. Executes tools if needed (with approval handling) 4. Observes tool results and incorporates them 5. Decides if more actions are needed or provides final response

The agent handles: - Tool execution with risk-based approval - Multi-step reasoning and tool chaining - Streaming responses - Error recovery - Safety limits (max iterations)

Parameters:

  • client (OllamaClient)

  • registry (ToolRegistry)

  • console (ARIAConsole)

  • approval_handler (ApprovalHandler | None)

  • max_iterations (int)

  • conversation_store (ConversationStore | None)

__init__(client, registry, console, approval_handler=None, max_iterations=10, conversation_store=None)[source]

Initialize the agent.

Parameters:

  • client (OllamaClient) – Ollama client for LLM calls

  • registry (ToolRegistry) – Tool registry for available tools

  • console (ARIAConsole) – Console for user interaction

  • approval_handler (ApprovalHandler | None) – Handler for tool approvals (creates default if None)

  • max_iterations (int) – Maximum number of ReAct loop iterations

  • conversation_store (ConversationStore | None) – Optional conversation store for history persistence

async start_session(session_id=None, title=None)[source]

Start a new session or resume an existing one.

Parameters:

  • session_id (str | None) – Optional session ID to resume. If None, creates new session.

  • title (str | None) – Optional title for new session

Returns:

The session ID

Return type:

str

Raises:

AgentError – If conversation store is not configured

async chat(user_message)[source]

Process a message with automatic history persistence.

This is a convenience method that: 1. Loads conversation history from the current session 2. Saves the user message 3. Runs the agent 4. Saves the assistant response and tool calls 5. Returns the response

Parameters:

user_message (str) – The user’s input message

Returns:

The agent’s response

Return type:

str

Raises:

AgentError – If no session is active or conversation store not configured

async run(user_message, conversation_history=None)[source]

Run the agent on a user message.

Executes the ReAct loop: 1. Build context with system prompt and history 2. Call LLM with available tools 3. If tool calls in response:

  • Execute tools (with approval)

  • Add results to context

  • Call LLM again with results

  • Repeat until no more tool calls or max iterations

  1. Return final text response and tool call records

Parameters:

  • user_message (str) – The user’s input message

  • conversation_history (list[ChatMessage] | None) – Previous conversation messages (optional)

Returns:

The agent’s final response and tool call records

Return type:

tuple[str, list[ToolCallRecord]]

Raises:

AgentError – If agent execution fails

async stream_response(user_message, conversation_history=None)[source]

Stream the agent’s response in real-time.

Note: This is a simpler version that doesn’t support tool use yet. For tool-using responses, use run() instead.

Parameters:

  • user_message (str) – The user’s input message

  • conversation_history (list[ChatMessage] | None) – Previous conversation messages (optional)

Yields:

str – Chunks of the response

Return type:

AsyncIterator[str]

Planner

Task planning and analysis for the ARIA agent.

This module provides simple task analysis to help the agent understand user requests and plan appropriate responses.

Executor

Tool execution with approval handling for the ARIA agent.

This module provides the ToolExecutor class which handles executing tools with the appropriate approval flows based on risk level.

exception aria.agent.executor.ToolExecutionError[source]

Bases: Exception

Exception raised when tool execution fails.

class aria.agent.executor.ToolExecutor(registry, approval_handler, console)[source]

Bases: object

Executes tools with risk-based approval handling.

The executor manages the complete lifecycle of tool execution: 1. Tool lookup and validation 2. Parameter validation 3. Risk assessment and approval (if needed) 4. Execution 5. Result formatting and display

Parameters:

  • registry (ToolRegistry)

  • approval_handler (ApprovalHandler)

  • console (ARIAConsole)

__init__(registry, approval_handler, console)[source]

Initialize the tool executor.

Parameters:

  • registry (ToolRegistry) – Tool registry for looking up tools

  • approval_handler (ApprovalHandler) – Handler for user approvals

  • console (ARIAConsole) – Console for displaying execution progress

async execute(tool_name, arguments)[source]
